question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is launching her second Cat III AIF, 'Kanishka Alpha'. With the compliance officer she is finalising service providers. As per current SEBI (AIF) Regulations (amended w.e.f. January 5, 2024), appointment of a SEBI-registered Custodian is:

answer.text: Optional, provided the Fund Administrator undertakes settlement responsibilities.
Compulsory for all AIFs — Cat I, II and III — and the custodian must be appointed prior to the date of first investment of the scheme.
Required only if the corpus exceeds INR 500 crore.
Required only for Cat III AIFs that trade in commodity derivatives.

explanation.text: The Logic: Post the SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations 2024 w.e.f. 5-Jan-2024, the Sponsor or Manager of AIFs shall COMPULSORILY appoint a custodian for safekeeping of securities, and per the SEBI circular dated 12-Jan-2024, the custodian must be in place BEFORE the first investment of the scheme. This is category-agnostic. The Trap: Option A confuses fund administration with custody — Fund Admin is not a regulated function in India. Option C reflects the PRE-2024 threshold-based rule that has been replaced. Option D applies only to the commodity-derivative sub-clause. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B pre-2024 still carries the old INR 500-cr threshold in legacy question banks — managers must know the updated rule. In XXI-B, PMS has its own custodian requirement under PMS Regulations 2020. Manager's Pro-Tip: Sign the custodian agreement BEFORE your first drawdown notice. LPs will condition their wire transfer on a live custodian account number — no custodian, no cash.
